purpose: Evidence-safe Miyoko Takaoka versus Masanori Hikichi composer-grammar calibration for the Sonic 3 Cube lineage.
external_tag_policy: External artist tags locate candidate controls only. They never establish composition, arrangement, programming, or authorship.

blind_protocol.feature_boundary: SPC runtime execution, persistent-part recovery, motif extraction, and the full pairwise similarity matrix are produced before creator identity is joined.
blind_protocol.freeze_boundary: The creator-blind matrix is frozen and hashed before evidence admissions or historical candidate labels enter evaluation.
blind_protocol.same_soundtrack_diagnostic: Leave-one-cue-out evaluation may use controls from the same soundtrack, but is diagnostic only because game, engine, sample-bank, collaborator, or implementation context can remain shared.
blind_protocol.strict_transfer_rule: A creator-facing transfer result requires removing every grounded cue from the query soundtrack before ranking and requires complete candidate coverage after that exclusion. Missing candidate coverage is insufficient evidence, never a zero score.
blind_protocol.team_world_rule: Team-level or partial-participation corpora may report candidate affinity and partition structure but cannot produce correctness or authorship labels without exact cue-level grounding.
blind_protocol.stress_holdout_rule: Uncertain retrospective clues, jointly composed cues, disputed cue mappings, and third-party decoys are never composer training controls. They exist to pressure-test the frozen geometry after reveal.
blind_protocol.reveal_reproducibility: The reveal records the SHA-256 of the frozen matrix and should also bind the exact panel, admission, and policy inputs used for the reveal.

masanori_hikichi.reason: All current strong Hikichi composer admissions are Terranigma cues. Same-soundtrack discrimination is informative but cannot establish cross-soundtrack Hikichi grammar until an independent exact Hikichi composer world is grounded.

calibration_strategy.within_game_boundary: Use individually grounded Takaoka and Hikichi cues from the same soundtrack to suppress game, platform, engine, sample-bank, and production-context shortcuts.
calibration_strategy.cross_game_boundary: Require creator-facing relations to survive independent soundtrack worlds. Team-level, partial-participation, and implementation-only corpora are evaluation or confound worlds, not automatic composer supervision.
calibration_strategy.cross_platform_boundary: Prefer shared musical abstractions that can survive SPC700, YM2151, YM2608, HuC6280, and Mega Drive realizations. A chip- or driver-specific signature cannot by itself become composer evidence.
calibration_strategy.sonic3_boundary: Only after those controls survive may the same composer-facing structural relations be evaluated on Sonic 3 Cube candidates.
calibration_strategy.role_firewall: Realization, sample, patch, envelope, driver, programming, and implementation similarity remains non-composer evidence unless separately role-grounded.

shared_composition_holdouts.reason: Jointly credited composition; useful shared-style or negative control, not an individual-class training example.

disputed_mapping_holdouts.fixture_path: tests/corpus/terranigma-spc/20 - Firm Steps Upon the Land.spc
disputed_mapping_holdouts.source_a: Tenchi Souzou Creative Soundtracks KTCR-1344 transcription credits original-version track 25 Firm Steps Upon the Land to Masanori Hikichi
disputed_mapping_holdouts.source_b: MusicBrainz gamerip maps the recording of the corresponding Japanese work to Masanori Hikichi and Miyoko Takaoka jointly
disputed_mapping_holdouts.reason: The sources disagree at the exact gamerip-to-work/composer mapping boundary. Exclude from grounding until reconciled rather than selecting the convenient label.

evaluation_only_clues.reason: Takaoka recalled that the OP may have been Hikichi's, but explicitly expressed uncertainty. Do not use as grounding supervision.

unmapped_direct_clues.reason: Direct creator statement exists, but the exact committed SPC fixture has not been identified confidently enough for admission.

third_party_decoys.reason: Documented non-Takaoka/non-Hikichi Terranigma contribution; useful to test whether a model is learning soundtrack identity instead of creator grammar.

work_level_single_composer_validation.evidence: Ghox game-level music credit identifies Miyoko Takaoka as the music contributor; VGMRips likewise identifies her as composer.
work_level_single_composer_validation.usage: Strong independent work-level validation. Do not auto-create exact-fixture admissions until the game-level credit-to-each-fixture inheritance is explicitly recorded.

derivative_inheritance_candidates.evidence: Takaoka's own Cube-era works list names Wizardry I・II. The earlier PC Engine Wizardry I・II pack identifies Takaoka as composer and contains these same three named cues; Wizardry III・IV credits both KK CUBE and Hisashi Matsushita and repeats the three cues at its head.
derivative_inheritance_candidates.usage: High-value same-work/cross-release inheritance hypothesis. Verify event or musical equivalence before promotion; do not use the local artist tags alone as proof.

team_or_partial_participation.evidence: Game credit is B.G.M. Composer: CUBE; Takaoka's own Cube-era works list names the title.
team_or_partial_participation.usage: Blind partition / validation world only until exact cue authorship is recovered.

team_or_partial_participation.evidence: Sound is credited to CUBE and Takaoka's own works list names the title; other contributors are possible.
team_or_partial_participation.usage: Partial-participation validation, not whole-set Takaoka supervision.

team_or_partial_participation.evidence: Battle Master has multiple surviving sound contributors including Masanori Hikichi; whole-set local artist tagging is therefore too coarse.
team_or_partial_participation.usage: Blind partition / validation world, not whole-set Hikichi supervision.

team_or_partial_participation.evidence: Takaoka's own Cube-era discography names Ecology Magic; the preserved VGMRips set labels her composer but notes that the instruction-manual credits were not available for checking.
team_or_partial_participation.usage: Promising cross-platform composer-grammar validation, but keep below exact grounding until primary/official cue or work-level credits are found.

team_or_partial_participation.evidence: Local tags identify Takaoka; CUBE preservation sources list Kakinoki Shogi as an uncredited CUBE work, while Takaoka's own list only says an unspecified shogi game among her Cube-era work.
team_or_partial_participation.usage: Weak identity-resolution world. Do not equate the unnamed shogi-game recollection with this exact title without additional evidence.

arrangement_or_implementation_only.evidence: Genesis credits Music and FX to CUBE; other versions directly credit Hiki as sound programmer, while track metadata also names David Javelosa and Masayuki Nagao.
arrangement_or_implementation_only.usage: Useful implementation/arrangement handwriting control; do not treat the whole Genesis soundtrack as Hikichi composition.

arrangement_or_implementation_only.evidence: Hikichi is credited as Sound Creator; the musical composition/arrangement lineage is separately credited.
arrangement_or_implementation_only.usage: Implementation/sound-production evidence only unless exact composition evidence emerges.

arrangement_or_implementation_only.work: Ys IV: Mask of the Sun
arrangement_or_implementation_only.evidence: Takaoka's own works list explicitly says arrangement only; game credits place CUBE members in sound-manipulation roles.
arrangement_or_implementation_only.usage: Arrangement realization control, never a Takaoka composer control by default.

special_confound.source: Terranigma Creative Soundtracks composer liner notes
special_confound.description: Takaoka wrote that Hikichi helped improve the sound quality of her compositions during development. Therefore Hikichi-like realization or timbral traits may occur in Takaoka-composed cues and must not be promoted to composer evidence.
